question: Where are contraceptive implants typically placed in the human body?
explanation: Contraceptive implants are designed to be placed just beneath the skin in the inner upper arm for easy access and removal. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h1)

question: What is the primary advantage of contraceptive implants over oral contraceptive pills?

options.A: They protect against all sexually transmitted infections
options.B: They do not require daily adherence from the user
options.C: They provide permanent sterilization after one year
options.D: They can be inserted and removed by the client alone

explanation: Long-acting reversible contraceptives eliminate the risk of user error associated with forgetting to take daily pills. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h1)

question: How does progestin in implants primarily block sperm from reaching an egg?

options.B: By destroying sperm in the vagina
options.C: By paralyzing the flagella of the sperm
options.D: By neutralizing the pH of the uterus

explanation: The progestin hormone creates a thick cervical plug that effectively prevents sperm from ascending into the uterus. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h2)

question: The endometrial changes caused by progestin-only implants achieve which primary effect?

options.A: Triggering immediate menopause in young women
options.B: Stimulating excessive muscular contractions of the womb
options.C: Shedding the entire endometrium every two weeks
options.D: Making the uterine lining unfavorable for implantation

explanation: Progestin thins the endometrium, preventing a fertilized egg from successfully embedding in the uterine wall. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h2)

question: How many rods make up the Implanon NXT contraceptive implant?
explanation: Implanon NXT consists of a single etonogestrel-releasing rod designed for three years of continuous use. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h3)

question: What is the active hormone found in the Jadelle contraceptive implant?
explanation: Jadelle is a two-rod implant that uses the progestin levonorgestrel for up to five years of protection. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h3)

question: A client with which condition should generally NOT receive a progestin-only implant?
explanation: Breast cancer is a formal contraindication for hormonal contraceptives because many breast tumors are hormone-sensitive. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h4)

question: A breastfeeding mother comes to the clinic six weeks postpartum asking for an implant. What is the appropriate action?

options.A: Wait until she has completed at least six months of exclusive breastfeeding
options.B: Provide the implant since progestin-only methods are safe during lactation
options.C: Advise her to use only barrier methods for the next year
options.D: Refuse the method until she stops breastfeeding completely

explanation: Progestin-only implants do not affect breast milk production and are safe to initiate postpartum, even during lactation. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h4)

question: What is the most common reason clients request early removal of their contraceptive implant?

options.A: Severe pain at the insertion site

explanation: Unpredictable spotting, prolonged bleeding, or amenorrhea often surprise clients if not properly discussed during pre-insertion counseling. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h5)

question: Which action is essential before proceeding with the insertion of any contraceptive implant?
explanation: Providers must confirm the client is not pregnant before placing an implant to avoid any potential exposure of an early pregnancy to progestin. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h5)

question: What layer of the skin is the target for correct contraceptive implant placement?
explanation: Implants must be placed just under the skin in the subdermal space to ensure they can be easily felt and removed later. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h6)

question: Why is deep placement of a contraceptive implant dangerous during the insertion procedure?

options.A: It completely stops the release of the progestin hormone
options.B: It triggers immediate systemic allergic reactions
options.C: It risks damage to underlying nerves and blood vessels
options.D: It causes the implant to dissolve within a few weeks

explanation: Placing the rod too deeply in the arm increases the chance of injuring major nerves and blood vessels and makes removal extremely difficult. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h6)

question: A client complains that she has stopped seeing her period entirely three months after getting an implant. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Send her to the laboratory for emergency kidney function tests
options.B: Prescribe high-dose estrogen pills to force regular monthly bleeding
options.C: Explain that absence of menstruation is a common and harmless effect of the hormone
options.D: Remove the implant immediately because it causes permanent infertility

explanation: Amenorrhea caused by progestin thinning the uterine lining is safe and does not mean blood is trapped inside the body. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common minor side effect of progestin-only implants?
explanation: Paralysis is not a side effect of contraceptive implants; side effects are generally limited to bleeding changes, headaches, and site tenderness. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h7)

question: What immediate post-insertion instruction should be given regarding the insertion site bandage?

options.A: Apply hot water compresses to the site every two hours
options.B: Remove the pressure bandage immediately after leaving the clinic room
options.C: Keep the area clean and dry for at least 24 hours
options.D: Scrub the incision site with medicated soap twice a day

explanation: Keeping the wound dry for the first day prevents bacteria from entering and reduces the risk of local infection. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h8)

question: What self-care check is recommended for a client who just received a single-rod implant?

options.A: Applying a tight elastic sleeve over the arm for three full months
options.B: Checking her temperature every morning for signs of systemic fever
options.C: Palpating the arm periodically to confirm the rod is still in place
options.D: Massaging the implant daily to help it settle deeper into the muscle

explanation: Clients are advised to gently feel for the implant under their skin to assure themselves that the device has not migrated or expelled. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h8)
